premises: Alloying additions (Mo, Si, B) refine the microstructure of HEAs.
Refined multiphase microstructure promotes formation of a stable, low-defect passive oxide film.
A stable, low-defect passive film reduces localized breakdown under mechanical stress and chloride attack.
Reduced localized breakdown leads to lower wear rate and corrosion current density.
The effect holds in moderate chloride solutions where the passive film remains stable.
